title.Full Title: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group phase 3 study of the efficacy and safety of Glyvantra (GLV-12) 5 mg and 10 mg once daily in adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin

design.Population Diagnosis or Condition: Type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled on metformin
design.Control Description: Matching placebo tablets once daily, added on to metformin
design.Randomisation Type: Block randomisation 1:1:1 through an interactive response technology system.
design.Site Geographic Scope: United States, Japan, Germany, India and Brazil
design.Blinded Roles: Participant, investigator, outcomes assessor, sponsor study team
design.Total Planned Duration of Trial Particip: Up to 34 weeks with visit windows (screening up to 3 weeks, 26 weeks of treatment, follow-up 4 weeks after the last dose)

arms.name: GLV-12 5 mg
arms.intervention: GLV-12 5 mg orally once daily for 26 weeks, with metformin

arms.name: GLV-12 10 mg
arms.intervention: GLV-12 10 mg orally once daily for 26 weeks, with metformin

arms.name: Placebo
arms.intervention: Matching placebo orally once daily for 26 weeks, with metformin

interventions.name: Metformin (background)
interventions.dose: at least 1500 mg a day, the participant’s own stable dose

objectives.text: To show that GLV-12 lowers HbA1c more than placebo after 26 weeks in adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin
To assess the safety and tolerability of GLV-12 5 mg and 10 mg over 26 weeks

endpoints.text: Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 26
Treatment-emergent adverse events; change in ALT, AST, creatinine and fasting glucose; vital signs

estimands.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin (HbA1c 7.0% to 10.5%)
estimands.treatment: GLV-12 5 mg or 10 mg once daily vs placebo for 26 weeks, added on to metformin

intercurrentEvents.name: Permanent discontinuation of trial intervention
intercurrentEvents.description: The HbA1c the participant would have had at Week 26 had they continued treatment.

intercurrentEvents.name: Start of rescue therapy
intercurrentEvents.description: The HbA1c the participant would have had without rescue; values after rescue are not used.

estimands.estimator: ANCOVA of the change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 26 with treatment as a factor and baseline HbA1c as a covariate; least-squares mean differences from placebo with 95% confidence intervals. A mixed model for repeated measures (treatment, visit, treatment by visit, baseline and baseline by visit; unstructured covariance) is the supplementary analysis.
estimands.missing: Values missing after discontinuation or rescue are assumed missing at random, consistent with the hypothetical strategy.
estimands.sensitivity: Placebo-based (reference-based) multiple imputation of missing Week 26 values, then ANCOVA, combined with Rubin’s rules.

narrative.13: ANCOVA: analysis of covariance. eGFR: estimated glomerular filtration rate. HbA1c: glycated haemoglobin. ITT: intent to treat. MMRM: mixed model for repeated measures. TEAE: treatment-emergent adverse event.
narrative.14: ICH E6(R3) Guideline for good clinical practice. ICH E9(R1) Addendum on estimands and sensitivity analysis. ICH M11 Clinical electronic Structured Harmonised Protocol.
narrative.2.1: Glyvantra (GLV-12) is an once-daily oral glucose transport modulator (a fictional class). This trial asks whether Glyvantra (GLV-12) is more effective than placebo in type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin, and how safe it is, over 26 weeks.
narrative.2.2.1: Identified and potential risks come from the nonclinical studies and earlier clinical trials summarised in the investigator's brochure. Each is mitigated by the eligibility criteria (section 5), the safety assessments in the schedule of activities (section 8.4) and the discontinuation rules (section 7.1).
narrative.2.2.2: Participants may benefit from improvement in their type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin. All participants receive standard care for their condition, and rescue therapy is available.
narrative.2.2.3: With the mitigations described, the sponsor considers the expected benefits to justify the risks.
narrative.4.1: This is a double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled trial with 3 arms (GLV-12 5 mg, GLV-12 10 mg, placebo), allocated 1:1:1, added on to metformin. Each dose is tested for superiority over placebo. Screening lasts up to 21 days, treatment 26 weeks and follow-up 4 weeks after the last dose. 90 participants are randomised.
narrative.4.2.1: The primary estimand uses a hypothetical strategy for permanent discontinuation of trial intervention and a hypothetical strategy for start of rescue therapy: the question is whether participants achieve the endpoint (change from baseline in hba1c at week 26) under the treatment as it is used, counting those who needed rescue or stopped treatment as not having benefited where the strategy says so.
narrative.4.2.2: A parallel group design is used because the condition can change over the treatment period and the effect is not expected to wash out quickly, so a cross-over design would not be reliable.
narrative.4.2.3: Placebo control is needed to distinguish the effect of the intervention from the natural course of the condition and from expectation. Participants may use rescue therapy, so no one is left without treatment.
narrative.4.2.4: 26 weeks of treatment is the duration regulators expect for the HbA1c endpoint, as HbA1c reflects about three months of glycaemia; 4 weeks of follow-up covers the 30-day window for treatment-emergent adverse events.
narrative.4.3: The sponsor may stop the trial, or an arm, on the recommendation of the independent data monitoring committee, for unacceptable risk, or if new information changes the benefit-risk balance.
narrative.4.4: The trial starts when the first participant signs informed consent. A participant has completed the trial at the Follow-up visit. The end of the trial is the last visit of the last participant.
narrative.4.5: Participants who complete the trial may enter the open-label extension study if it is open at their site. Otherwise the investigator arranges standard care.
narrative.5.1: Adults aged 18 to 75 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled on metformin. Women and men are included; the age range covers the population that will use the product.
narrative.5.6: A participant who does not meet the criteria is a screen failure; the reason is recorded. A participant may be rescreened once, after at least 4 weeks, with a new participant number and new consent.
narrative.6.1: GLV-12 5 mg: 5 mg film-coated tablet, oral, once daily, for 26 weeks. GLV-12 10 mg: 10 mg film-coated tablet, oral, once daily, for 26 weeks. Placebo tablets match the active tablets in appearance.
narrative.6.2: The doses were chosen from the exposure-response analysis of the earlier trial, which showed a plateau of effect at the higher dose and acceptable safety at both.
narrative.6.3: One tablet is taken by mouth each morning with water, with or without food. A missed dose is skipped if more than 12 hours late.
narrative.6.5: There is no antidote. In case of overdose the participant is monitored and treated symptomatically; the overdose is recorded as a special safety situation (9.4).
narrative.6.6: Trial intervention is stored at 20 to 25 °C in a locked area with access limited to authorised staff. The site records every bottle received, dispensed, returned and destroyed (6.6.3 Accountability).
narrative.6.7: Participants are randomised through the interactive response technology system on Day 1. Block randomisation 1:1:1 through an interactive response technology system. The participant, investigator, assessors and sponsor study team are blinded. The investigator can unblind a participant through the system in an emergency.
narrative.6.8: Adherence is checked by counting tablets returned at each visit; less than 80% or more than 120% of expected tablets is a deviation.
narrative.6.10: Prohibited: any glucose-lowering medicine other than metformin and rescue therapy, and systemic corticosteroids for more than 7 days. Strong inhibitors of CYP3A4 are prohibited because they raise GLV-12 exposure (a possible interaction). All concomitant therapy is recorded.
narrative.7.1: The trial intervention is stopped permanently for a confirmed fasting glucose above 15 mmol/L, an eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2, ALT above 3 × ULN with total bilirubin above 2 × ULN, pregnancy, or if the investigator judges it in the participant’s interest. Participants who stop stay in the trial and attend every visit.
narrative.7.2: A participant may withdraw at any time. Data collected until withdrawal are kept. The site asks, but cannot require, a final safety visit.
narrative.7.3: Before a participant is called lost to follow-up, the site makes at least three attempts by telephone and one by letter, and records them.
narrative.8.1: Procedures follow the schedule of activities (1.3). Laboratory samples are taken fasting. Each participant receives diabetes education on Day 1 and at Week 4 (diet, physical activity, foot care, recognising hypoglycaemia); sessions are recorded in a study-specific form.
narrative.8.2: At screening: consent, demographics, medical history, eligibility, vital signs and laboratory tests. Day 1 assessments before the first dose are the baseline.
narrative.8.3: HbA1c is measured at the central laboratory (Meridian Central Laboratories, fictional) at screening and Weeks 4, 12 and 26, by an NGSP-certified method.
narrative.8.4: Vital signs (8.4.2), clinical laboratory tests (8.4.4, listed in 12.1) and, for participants of childbearing potential, pregnancy tests (8.4.5) are done at the visits in 1.3.
narrative.9.1: An adverse event is any untoward medical occurrence in a participant, whether or not related to the trial intervention. A serious adverse event results in death, is life-threatening, requires or prolongs hospitalisation, results in persistent disability, is a congenital anomaly, or is another important medical event.
narrative.9.2: 9.2.1 Timing: adverse events are collected from the signing of informed consent until the follow-up visit. Serious adverse events are reported to the sponsor within 24 hours of the site becoming aware. Hypoglycaemia is recorded on the adverse event form with the glucose value.
narrative.10.1: Tests are two-sided at a significance level of 0.05. The statistical analysis plan, finalised before unblinding, gives the details.
narrative.10.2: Intent-to-treat population: All randomised participants, analysed as randomised. Safety population: All randomised participants who took at least one dose, analysed as treated.
narrative.10.3: Demographics and baseline characteristics are summarised by arm with descriptive statistics.
narrative.10.4: The change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 26 is analysed in the intent-to-treat population with ANCOVA (treatment as a factor, baseline HbA1c as a covariate), on observed values after excluding values after rescue or discontinuation. Supplementary: an MMRM over all visits. Sensitivity: placebo-based multiple imputation. Subgroups (age, sex, region, baseline HbA1c below or at least 8.5%) are shown in a forest plot.
narrative.10.5: Treatment-emergent adverse events; change in ALT, AST, creatinine and fasting glucose; vital signs: summarised descriptively by arm (see 10.7).
narrative.10.7: Adverse events are coded with MedDRA. Treatment-emergent adverse events are those starting on or after the first dose and no later than 30 days after the last dose; they are summarised by arm in the safety population, with time to the first treatment-emergent adverse event by Kaplan-Meier. Laboratory values are shown as shift tables and vital signs by analysis window.
narrative.10.10: The two doses are tested in a fixed sequence: GLV-12 10 mg against placebo first, at two-sided 0.05; GLV-12 5 mg only if the 10 mg test is significant. This keeps the familywise type I error rate at 0.05.
narrative.10.11: A sample size of 90 randomised participants (30 per arm) gives 80% power to detect a difference of 0.8% in the change from baseline in HbA1c between a dose of GLV-12 and placebo (standard deviation 1.0%, two-sided alpha 0.05), allowing for 15% of participants without a Week 26 value.
narrative.11.1: The trial follows the protocol, ICH E6(R3) good clinical practice, the Declaration of Helsinki and the applicable regulations, including Regulation (EU) No 536/2014, 21 CFR parts 50, 56 and 312, and the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019. Each site starts only after its ethics committee approves.
narrative.11.2: The investigator conducts the trial at the site and supervises delegated staff. The sponsor monitors the trial and ensures direct access to source records for monitoring, audits and inspections.
narrative.11.3: The investigator or a delegate explains the trial and gives the participant time to ask questions before consent is signed. Consent is renewed when new information may affect willingness to continue.
narrative.11.4: An independent data monitoring committee of two clinicians and a statistician reviews unblinded safety data every 6 months, under a charter that accompanies the protocol. It recommends to the sponsor whether to continue, change or stop the trial.
narrative.11.5: The sponsor holds insurance that covers participants for harm caused by taking part, as the law of each country requires.
narrative.11.6: Critical-to-quality factors are the primary endpoint assessment, eligibility and safety reporting. Centralised monitoring of key risk indicators and targeted on-site review focus on them.
narrative.11.7: Data are entered in a validated electronic data capture system with an audit trail; laboratory and randomisation data are transferred electronically and reconciled.
narrative.11.8: Participants are identified by number only. Personal data are processed under the applicable data protection laws; a breach is reported to the sponsor within 24 hours and handled under its procedure.
narrative.11.9: Source records are the medical records and the worksheets defined in the monitoring plan; data entered directly in the eCRF are identified in advance.
narrative.11.10: Protocol deviations are recorded in the eCRF and classified as important or not, following the deviation plan.
narrative.11.11: The sponsor or the investigator may close a site for poor recruitment, poor compliance with the protocol or good clinical practice, or safety reasons.
narrative.11.12: Results are posted in the public registries within one year of the end of the trial and submitted for publication whatever the outcome.
narrative.6.9: 6.9.1 Background therapy: metformin at the participant’s stable dose of at least 1500 mg a day, unchanged during the trial. 6.9.2 Rescue therapy: Rescue therapy (a sulfonylurea or basal insulin, by local practice) is started for fasting glucose above 13.3 mmol/L (240 mg/dL) after Week 4 or above 11.1 mmol/L (200 mg/dL) after Week 12, confirmed on a second sample.
narrative.12.1: Central laboratory (Meridian Central Laboratories, fictional): HbA1c; chemistry: ALT, AST, creatinine with eGFR (CKD-EPI), total cholesterol, fasting glucose. Samples are destroyed after analysis; none are kept for future research.

statements.10.11: A sample size of 90 randomised participants (30 per arm) gives 80% power to detect a difference of 0.8% in the change from baseline in HbA1c between a dose of GLV-12 and placebo (standard deviation 1.0%, two-sided alpha 0.05), allowing for 15% of participants without a Week 26 value.

data.multiplicity: The two doses are tested in a fixed sequence: GLV-12 10 mg against placebo first, at two-sided 0.05; GLV-12 5 mg only if the 10 mg test is significant. This keeps the familywise type I error rate at 0.05.
data.rescue: Rescue therapy (a sulfonylurea or basal insulin, by local practice) is started for fasting glucose above 13.3 mmol/L (240 mg/dL) after Week 4 or above 11.1 mmol/L (200 mg/dL) after Week 12, confirmed on a second sample.

narrative.11.4: An independent data monitoring committee of two clinicians and a statistician reviews unblinded safety data every 6 months, under a charter that accompanies the protocol. It recommends to the sponsor whether to continue, change or stop the trial.
narrative.11.5: The sponsor holds insurance that covers participants for harm caused by taking part, as the law of each country requires.
narrative.11.6: Critical-to-quality factors are the primary endpoint assessment, eligibility and safety reporting. Centralised monitoring of key risk indicators and targeted on-site review focus on them.
narrative.11.7: Data are entered in a validated electronic data capture system with an audit trail; laboratory and randomisation data are transferred electronically and reconciled.
narrative.11.8: Participants are identified by number only. Personal data are processed under the applicable data protection laws; a breach is reported to the sponsor within 24 hours and handled under its procedure.
narrative.11.9: Source records are the medical records and the worksheets defined in the monitoring plan; data entered directly in the eCRF are identified in advance.
narrative.11.10: Protocol deviations are recorded in the eCRF and classified as important or not, following the deviation plan.
narrative.11.11: The sponsor or the investigator may close a site for poor recruitment, poor compliance with the protocol or good clinical practice, or safety reasons.
narrative.11.12: Results are posted in the public registries within one year of the end of the trial and submitted for publication whatever the outcome.
narrative.6.9: 6.9.1 Background therapy: metformin at the participant’s stable dose of at least 1500 mg a day, unchanged during the trial. 6.9.2 Rescue therapy: Rescue therapy (a sulfonylurea or basal insulin, by local practice) is started for fasting glucose above 13.3 mmol/L (240 mg/dL) after Week 4 or above 11.1 mmol/L (200 mg/dL) after Week 12, confirmed on a second sample.
narrative.12.1: Central laboratory (Meridian Central Laboratories, fictional): HbA1c; chemistry: ALT, AST, creatinine with eGFR (CKD-EPI), total cholesterol, fasting glucose. Samples are destroyed after analysis; none are kept for future research.

statements.10.11: A sample size of 90 randomised participants (30 per arm) gives 80% power to detect a difference of 0.8% in the change from baseline in HbA1c between a dose of GLV-12 and placebo (standard deviation 1.0%, two-sided alpha 0.05), allowing for 15% of participants without a Week 26 value.

data.multiplicity: The two doses are tested in a fixed sequence: GLV-12 10 mg against placebo first, at two-sided 0.05; GLV-12 5 mg only if the 10 mg test is significant. This keeps the familywise type I error rate at 0.05.
data.rescue: Rescue therapy (a sulfonylurea or basal insulin, by local practice) is started for fasting glucose above 13.3 mmol/L (240 mg/dL) after Week 4 or above 11.1 mmol/L (200 mg/dL) after Week 12, confirmed on a second sample.

amendment.summary: Exclusion criterion EX01 lowered from an eGFR below 45 to below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2, in line with current metformin prescribing information, which allows metformin down to an eGFR of 30; sites reported screening failures of otherwise eligible participants.
amendment.safetyRights: No: participants with an eGFR of 30 to 44 can take metformin under its prescribing information; renal function is monitored at every visit.
amendment.dataImpact: No: the primary endpoint and its analysis are unchanged; participants enrolled under each version are identifiable.

changes.rationale: Align eligibility with current metformin prescribing information (eGFR down to 30).
